classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the supplied kite diagram, identify the string as the hypotenuse, and rearrange a sine equation with the unknown denominator.

content.prompt: A kite is flying at a height of 27 m above the anchor point. If the string is inclined at $42^\circ$ to the horizontal, find the length of the string correct to the nearest metre.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 diagram beneath the kite problem
spec.description: Kite attached to the upper-left end of the string; dashed vertical height and horizontal baseline meet at a marked right angle. The string descends to the lower-right anchor, where the interior angle is 42 degrees. Ordinary source blue outlines and red construction lines are rendered in house black, retaining the dashed construction distinction.
spec.mathematics: The vertical height is 27 m, opposite the 42-degree angle at the anchor. The string is the hypotenuse. Triangle coordinates derive from height 3 coordinate units and horizontal distance 3/tan(42 degrees); the acute angle mark runs counterclockwise from the string to the leftward baseline.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the string length is not supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the string length. The height is opposite the $42^\circ$ angle and the string is the hypotenuse.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 42^\circ &= \frac{27}{x}\\x\sin 42^\circ &= 27\\x &= \frac{27}{\sin 42^\circ}\\x &\approx 40.351\\x &\approx 40\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre)}\end{align*}$$
